Heat Without Debate?

Climate change in the German Bundestag next to the physical climate signal and public attention, 2004-01 to 2026-09. Exploratory view of the pipeline outputs so far.

Provisional: “climate-related” means a sentence contains one of the 14 core keywords from config/keywords_de.yaml (simple substring match). This is a stand-in until step 2 (src/02_relevance.py) exists. Stance (step 3) is not available yet.

Google Trends, all four exports

Each file was exported alone, so each has its own 0–100 scale. Compare shapes, not levels across panels.

Klimawandel

Check the exports: “Klimawandel” jumps to 100 in 2022-04 and “Klimaschutz” in 2023-04 while the months around sit near 10. Single-month spikes like this are often sampling glitches; a re-export on another day would show whether they are real. They also lift the 12-month averages for a full year. “Klima” (topic) also covers weather and air conditioning, which may explain why it moves differently.

Notes and caveats

  • Speeches: PoliCorp-GermaParl2-PLUS (15th–20th Bundestag) plus the 21st Bundestag converted from Bundestag Open Data XML. Interjections excluded; speaker roles MPs, government, Bundesrat.
  • Climate relevance is a provisional keyword match on the core list only. Substring matching means e.g. “Klimaschutzgesetz” counts, but so would false hits. Replace with step 2 output.
  • Many protocols write CO₂ as “CO 2” (all of 2009, most of 2008, 2018 and 2019), which the keyword “co2” misses. This page treats “CO 2” as “co2”; step 2 needs the same fix.
  • The sentence share depends on how sentences are split; PoliCorp and the XML converter split slightly differently (not yet validated on this machine).
  • Correlations are descriptive Pearson coefficients on monthly data, not models. Time-series methods (detrending, lags, ARIMA/VAR) belong in the real analysis.
  • Google Trends values are sampled by Google; a re-export on another day can differ slightly.
  • Data ends 2026-09 (end_date in config/settings.yaml).
  • Rebuild the data: python viz/export_data.py, then npm run dev in viz/.
